newsitem.title: UK: Geomaque to up Mexico reserves next week.
newsitem.headline: Geomaque to up Mexico reserves next week.

text.p: Canadian gold miner Geomaque will announce next week an increase in reserves at its San Francisco mine in Mexico, officials said on Thursday.

Resources are expected to rise to approximately 1.6-1.7 million ounces from the present 1.2 million, but it was unclear how much of the rise would go into reserves, Vice President of Exploration Phillip Walford told Reuters after a presentation for mining analysts in London.
"We don't know yet exactly what it's going to be, the computers are still processing the data, but it could be 1.6 or 1.7 (million ounces)," Walford said, referring to resources.
Reserves were last increased to 525,000 ounces in April, when there were also 100,000 more ounces of inferred gold.
"At that time we did not have enough density of information to put it into reserves," Walford said.

Production will also be increased at the 100-percent owned San Francisco property -- Geomaque's only operating mine -- from the present target of 50,000 ounces per year, but a decision is not likely to be made in time for next week's announcement.
"It could be 60,000, 70,000 or maybe even 100,000 (ounces). It all depends on what we get next week," Walford said.
Production at San Francisco began in March and first half output was 16,330 ounces at an average cash cost of $215 per ounce.
Exploration is under way at other sites in Mexico and a resource calculation should be made for the La Chicharra property in the next couple of months.

Geomaque, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, plans to launch output at the Vueltas del Rio mine in Honduras in mid-1998, President and Chief Operating Officer John Paterson said during the presentation.
Output is expected to be 30,000 to 40,000 ounces per year from a reserve of 250,000 ounces.

Exploration will continue at the 10,000-hectare concession in northwesttern Honduras, the principal asset of Milagro Minerals Inc, which agreed to merge with Geomaque last month. Milagro shareholders are due to receive one Geomaque share for every four shares of Milagro held.
"Our shares will be diluted by about eight percent, but our reserves are increasing by 50 percent," Paterson said.
Drilling is due to begin at the firm's 500 sq km Kiapaga concession in Burkina Faso next month and assays should be ready by early 1997, Walford said.
